[wasm][tests] 用于构建 AOT 测试时 `EnableAggressiveTrimming` 错误的跟踪 issue

为启用通过 AOT 运行测试，我们需要使用 `$(EnableAggressiveTrimming)==true` 来缩短 AOT 构建时间。但启用它会引入一些构建问题或测试失败。- 这些问题带有 trimming-for-aot 标签。本地复现：1. `$ /dotnet.sh build /p:Configuration=Release /p:TargetOS=Browser /p:TargetArchitecture=wasm /t:Test /path/to/project/file /p:EnableAggressiveTrimming=true` 2. 如果无法通过上述方式复现，请在上述命令行中尝试添加 `/p:BuildAOTTestsOnHelix=true` 构建。3. 如果仍无法复现，请在 discord 频道提问，因为这可能是 helix 问题。提示：* 如果你正在处理该 issue，请务必将其分配给自己 * 可以添加 `/p:DebuggerSupport=true` 以获取行号

[browser][HybridGlobalization][tracking] Regressions of text APIs when running in *HybridGlobalization* mode.

Based on our investigations, some of the String, TextInfo and CompareInfo APIs are running slower with WASM *HybridGlobalization (HG)* enabled than with HG disabled. Here is the summary of the largest regressions. We compare the default behavior (using ICU4C) to the scenario with enabled HG (both running with interpreter, similar numbers are reported for AOT as well). | API | time ICU4C [ms] | time HG [ms] | slow-down | |-----------------------------|-----------------|--------------|-----------| | String, TextInfo ToLower | 0.2698 | 90.9531 | 33611% | | String, TextInfo ToUpper | 0.2545 | 90.9077 | 35620% | | String, TextInfo ToTitleCase | 7.1761 | 113.7647 | 1485% | | String, String Compare | 0.0397 | 0.374 | 842% | | String, String Equals | 0.0397 | 0.3717 | 836% | | String, CompareInfo Compare | 0.0393 | 0.373 | 849% | | String, String IndexOf | 4.7239 | 2362.6667 | 49915% | | String, String LastIndexOf | 8.1408 | 2361 | 28902% | Note: These regressions only influence application where HG is enabled (e.g., by adding `<HybridGlobalization>true</HybridGlobalization>` to the `.csproj` file) as it is not the default settings. --- Tracking list of APIs waiting to be optimize: ToLower ToUpper ToTitleCase Compare Equals IndexOf: reduced down to 38ms by [link] LastIndexOf: reduced down to 38ms by [link] --- cc: @ilonatommy @mkhamoyan @SamMonoRT

[Tracking] 为 Swift 调用约定实现 Mono 支持

描述 Swift 编程语言具有不同的 ABI、运行时环境和对象模型。本 issue 根据设计文档跟踪实现 Mono 对 Swift 调用约定支持的工作。根据该调用约定，self 上下文有专用寄存器，并且由于被频繁使用，始终通过它们传递。在同一对象上调用其他方法的方法可以共享 self 上下文。错误也通过寄存器处理，因此调用方需要检查错误并在必要时抛出。实现 P/Invoke thunk 应能通过在这些场景使用预定义寄存器集来简化寄存器调配。以下是需要实现的任务列表。请注意，issue 的拆分并不施加硬性截止日期。如果某些功能未能在特定预览版本中上游合入，本 issue 将相应更新。任务：为长度不超过 4 的序列实现 Frozen blittable struct lowering [link] [link]；为 Swift 调用约定实现 UnmanagedCallersOnly 支持；衡量直接 Swift 互操作的性能

Tracking Issue for `-Zlockfile-path`

Summary Original issue: #5707 Implementation: #14326 Documentation: [link] The `-Zlockfile-path` flag enables the `resolver.lockfile-path` configuration option, which allows you to specify the path of the lockfile `Cargo.lock`. Unresolved Issues Inconsistency in `resolver` table being applied to `cargo install` How this should work if the lockfile or a parent directory is not present - In [#14326], missing parent directories will be created when Cargo is about to write the lockfile. This minimizes the chance of creating dangling directories. `cargo install --lockfile-path=<path>` implies `--locked`, and requires the alternative lockfile to exist. - This behavior diverges from other commands, which allow the absence of lockfile at the alternative path. 15510 [#14326]: [link] Future Extensions _No response_ Tasks Add an unstable doc under <[link] #14423 `cargo install` should make `--lockfile-path` imply `--locked` #14556 Add support for `resolver.lockfile-path` in #16510 Expand `resolver.lockfile-path` coverage in #16617 Remove `--lockfile-path` in 1.95.0-nightly About tracking issues Tracking issues are used to record the overall progress of implementation. They are also used as hubs connecting to other relevant issues, e.g., bugs or open design questions. A tracking issue is however *not* meant for large scale discussion, questions, or bug reports about a feature. Instead, open a dedicated issue for the specific matter and add the relevant feature gate label.

Tracking Issue for credential-process RFC 2730

**Summary** RFC: [link] Implementation: #8934 Documentation: [link] Issues: [link] This feature provides a configuration option to specify a process to fetch a token to authenticate with a registry. **Unresolved issues** Is this approach useful enough? Things like macos keychain don't protect against being executed to extract tokens (and I don't see a way to require a password, or force the process to be untrusted). The lack of signatures also cause issues (each update of the toolchain will cause it to become untrusted again). * Making the built-in providers like `cargo:macos-keychain` part of the cargo binary improves security here, since only the Cargo binary is accessing the Keychain. If we get Cargo signed by Apple, then it would be further improved. Should the `login` API be changed? Providers that need to be interactive need to be able to read from stdin. * This is worked around by having the credential-provider re-open `stdin` from `/dev/tty` or `$CONIN` Should the storage key off the registry name? RFC 3139 discusses problems with this. RESOLVED: credential helpers are now keying off the index url via #10592. Should it be possible to pass additional arguments on the command line for `cargo login` that would be sent to the provider? E.g. `cargo login -- --extra-arg-for-provider` * Implemented in #12499 Figure out the name for `cargo:basic`: `cargo:token-from-stdout` Remove cargo-1password as a built-in (add the `fn main` so it can be published separately). Create a new `-Z` flag for `cargo:paseto`. Publish `cargo-credential-1password` to crates.io Figure out MSRV sup

TRACKING: Stabilize instrument advisory parameter: "Attributes"

**What are you trying to achieve?** Stabilize Instrument advisory parameter: Attributes. **Additional context.** These advisory parameters are important for the Java Instrumentation, where we have a unified API for recording spans/metrics (e.g. HTTP server spans / HTTP server metrics), and so we pass in a single set of attributes (the span attributes), and use this advisory parameter when we construct the metrics in order to provide a default attribute filter, and then users can create a metric view to override the default and stamp more or less of the span attributes onto the metric.

Tracking OTel Spec Issues for GA

Since the OTel Beta release, we've refined our spec issue tracking process based on the community's cadence, participation level, and responsibilities to help focus the community's efforts. This issue is to help explain how spec issues are tracked on our road to our first OTel GA release. This issue can be closed after the GA release and this description may be updated as required. Anybody may open a new spec issue, but the OTel Technical Committee (TC) is responsible for triaging the spec issue. At least one of the TC members is required to participate in the triage process. Issues may be triaged anytime after they are opened, but there are 2 dedicated times set aside for triage of new issues if nobody gets to them: * weekly spec sig mtg on tuesdays * weekly otel issue scrub mtg on fridays For an issue to be triaged, it should have github labels applied: * one of the release: labels * one of the priority: labels * at least one spec: label (usually one) * at least one area: label (usually one) The release: labels have the meaning: * release:required-for-ga automatically gets label priority:p1 to represent the highest priority issue that must resolve before GA. If triaged as such, there must be an `assignee` to own the progress of the issue towards resolution. * release:allowed-for-ga can only have priority label priority:p2 or priority:p3. These issues are optional to be resolved before GA, i.e they will not block a GA release.
